    if (sourceVertex == null || targetVertex == null) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source and target vertices must not be null");
    }
    if (e == null) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Edge must not be null");
    }

    // The graph maintains an index mapping each vertex to the set of incident edges.
    // Add the edge for both source and target vertices. If the vertex has no
    // entries yet, create a new set.
    try {
        // Assuming the class has a field named 'index' of type Map<V, Set<E>>
        // If the field does not exist, a compilation error will be thrown
        // indicating that the implementation needs adjustment.
        // The following uses computeIfAbsent to create the set lazily.
        java.util.Objects.requireNonNull(index, "Index map must be initialized in the graph implementation");
        index.computeIfAbsent(sourceVertex, v -> new java.util.HashSet<>()).add(e);
        index.computeIfAbsent(targetVertex, v -> new java.util.HashSet<>()).add(e);
    } catch (MissingFieldException | NoSuchFieldException | IllegalAccessException ex) {
        // If the expected index field is not available, throw an informative
        // runtime exception so that the caller knows the implementation is
        // incomplete and needs to supply the appropriate field.
        throw new RuntimeException("Graph implementation must provide an 'index' field of type Map<V, Set<E>>", ex);
    }
}
